items.stem: What does 'shifting security left' mean in DevSecOps?

options.text: Moving security checks earlier into development and the pipeline rather than only before release
options.rationale: Correct: earlier feedback is cheaper and faster to fix.

options.text: Delaying all security testing until production
options.rationale: That is shifting right, the opposite.

options.text: Assigning security to a single gatekeeper team
Disabling automated scans to move faster
options.rationale: That removes security, not shifts it left.

items.explanation: Correct: earlier feedback is cheaper and faster to fix.

items.stem: What is the purpose of Software Composition Analysis (SCA) in a pipeline?

options.text: Detecting known vulnerabilities in third-party and open-source dependencies
options.rationale: Correct: SCA inventories dependencies and flags known CVEs.

options.text: Scanning your own source code for logic bugs
Testing a running application from the outside

items.explanation: Correct: SCA inventories dependencies and flags known CVEs.

items.stem: Which practices make security gates sustainable in CI/CD? (Select TWO)

options.text: Fail builds on critical/high findings while triaging lower-severity ones
options.rationale: Correct: risk-based gating protects without blocking everything.

options.text: Scan for committed secrets automatically on every change
options.rationale: Correct: catching secrets early prevents leaks.

options.text: Block the build on every low-severity informational finding
options.rationale: False; that stalls delivery and breeds alert fatigue.

options.text: Store secrets in the repository for convenience
options.rationale: False; secrets must stay out of source control.

items.explanation: Correct: risk-based gating protects without blocking everything.; Correct: catching secrets early prevents leaks.
